verses.text: Don't envy people who do evil or wish you could run with them.
Their hearts plot violence, and their mouths talk about causing harm.
Wisdom builds a house. Understanding makes it stand firm.
Knowledge fills its rooms with rare and beautiful treasures.
A wise person has great power. A person with knowledge grows stronger,
because you need wise guidance to wage war, and victory comes with many advisers.
Wisdom is out of a fool's reach. At the city gate, they have nothing to say.
People will call anyone who plots evil a schemer.
Foolish schemes are sin. People can't stand a mocker.
If you give way when trouble hits, your strength is small.
Rescue people being led away to die. Hold back those staggering toward slaughter!
If you say, “We had no idea,” won't the one who weighs hearts see through that? Won't the one who guards your life know? Won't he repay each person for what they've done?
My son, eat honey, because it's good. Honey dripping from the comb tastes sweet. 🍯
That's what wisdom is like for your soul. If you find it, there's a reward ahead, and your hope won't be cut off.
You who do evil, don't lie in wait at the home of someone who does right. Don't wreck their place of rest.
A person who does right may fall seven times and still get up again. Disaster knocks the wicked down for good.
Don't celebrate when your enemy falls. Don't let your heart get glad when they're brought down.
The LORD might see it, be displeased, and turn his anger away from them.
Don't get worked up over people who do evil or envy the wicked.
An evildoer has no reward ahead. The lamp of the wicked will go out.
My son, revere the LORD and the king. Don't join up with rebels.
Disaster can rise up suddenly. Who knows what ruin may come from them both?
Here are more sayings from the wise. Playing favorites when you judge is wrong.
Tell a wicked person, “You're in the right,” and peoples will curse you and nations will despise you.
Things will go well for those who convict the guilty. They'll receive a rich blessing.
An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips.
Get your work outside in order and prepare your fields. Then build your house.
Don't testify against your neighbor without cause. Don't use your words to deceive.
Don't say, “I'll do to them what they did to me. I'll pay them back for what they did.”
I walked past a slacker's field, past the vineyard of someone who lacked understanding.
Thorns had taken over. Nettles covered the ground, and the stone wall had fallen apart.
I took a good look and thought it over. Here's what I learned:
a little more sleep, a little more dozing, a little folding of your hands to rest,
and poverty will come at you like a robber, and need like an armed man.
